slides.headline: On November 1, a state was born. Seventeen years later, on the same date, it got its modern name.
Karnataka Rajyotsava marks November 1, 1956 - the day Mysore State was formed under the States Reorganisation Act
slides.body: Kannada-speaking regions from Bombay, Madras, Hyderabad, and Coorg were merged into a single state, consolidating India's linguistic map through negotiation rather than conflict.

slides.headline: On November 1, 1973 - exactly 17 years later - Mysore State was renamed Karnataka.
slides.body: Chief Minister D. Devaraj Urs moved the renaming resolution. Today, Rajyotsava is marked with flag-hoisting and the Rajyotsava Awards honoring contributions to the state.

slides.eyebrow: Why it matters for Viksit Bharat 2047
slides.headline: A Viksit Bharat is still built the way Karnataka was - states joined by agreement, not by force.
slides.body: The linguistic reorganization of the 1950s laid the administrative groundwork for the diverse, unified country still being built today.
